title: From a Rational Recurrence to an Elliptic Curve: Non-Integrability, the Somos Bilinearization, and the Degeneration of the σ-Function Solution
content: We study the coupled second-order rational recurrence x(2k+2) = a11x(2k) + a12x(2k+1), x(2k+1) = a22x(2k−1) + a21/x2(2k−1) within the landscape of discrete integrable systems. Written as a planar map it is a skew product: the odd-indexed subsequence obeys an autonomous one-dimensional nonlinear map and the even-indexed subsequence is linear and slaved to it. We prove that for an open set of parameters every continuous first integral is constant on the basin of an attracting fixed point (numerically, almost all of the plane), and we classify the lower-dimensional loci on which weak, resonant, or linear invariants survive. We then contrast this with the Somos-4 and Somos-5 recurrences: giving self-contained derivations of their QRT reductions and conserved quantities, we show that the same algebraic nonlinearity becomes integrable precisely when it is recast in bilinear (Hirota) form [12]. We develop the elliptic-curve linearization for the full two-parameter family (α, β), computing the Weierstrass invariants g2, g3, j and the discriminant locus explicitly, and we give the corrected σ-function solution τn = ABn σ(z0 + nv)/(√(4α) σ(v))n2, in which the translation point is always g = 0 and ℘(v) = (J2 − 4β)/3. Two cases are worked to high precision: the classical sequence 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 23, … lives on the conductor-37 rank-one curve 37a1 with translation by the rational point (1, 0) of infinite order, while α = 2, β = 3 yields a different curve and is reconstructed exactly from σ. Finally we determine when the curve degenerates: on the discriminant locus Δ(J, α, β) = 0 the cubic acquires a repeated root, the fibre becomes a singular rational curve, and the σ-solution collapses to elementary form — hyperbolic or trigonometric at a node, purely rational τn = (an + b)γn2δn at a cusp — so that integrability persists but its elliptic transcendence is lost (and the Laurent integrality may fail).
